data.title: Pizza Calculations
data.statement:
Mark loves Pizza.

He grabs the flyer from his local pizza place from the fridge and checks their pizzas. 

The menu shows [[N]] pizzas in 3 sizes: {{22cm}} {{26cm}} {{32cm}} (diameter of round pizza) along with their respective prices.

Suddenly his analytical instinct kicks in and he wants to know <<which size is most cost efficient for each pizza on the list>>?

So he makes a list with pizza name and the size with the cheapest price per cm².

For this task Mark had to dig out his 8th grade math book and found the following formula:
`A = π ⋅ r², where r = d/2, d=diameter of a circle, A=area of a circle, and π≈3.1416.`

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Mark loves Pizza.

He grabs the flyer from his local pizza place from the fridge and checks their pizzas.

The menu shows N pizzas in 3 sizes: 22cm 26cm 32cm (diameter of round pizza) along with their respective prices.

Suddenly his analytical instinct kicks in and he wants to know which size is most cost efficient for each pizza on the list?

So he makes a list with pizza name and the size with the cheapest price per cm².

For this task Mark had to dig out his 8th grade math book and found the following formula:
A = π ⋅ r², where r = d/2, d=diameter of a circle, A=area of a circle, and π≈3.1416.
Input
Line 1: An integer N representing the number of pizzas on the menu
Next N lines: A space-separated string containing the pizza name name, followed by 3 floats price1 price2 price3 representing the prices for the 22cm, 26cm, and 32cm sizes respectively.
Output
N lines: For each pizza, output its name followed by a space and the size (22cm, 26cm, or 32cm) with the lowest price per cm².

Preserve the original order of the pizzas.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 100
1 ≤ length of name ≤ 99
0 < price1 ≤ 1000
0 < price2 ≤ 1000
0 < price3 ≤ 1000

name contains no space characters.
Each name appears once in each case.

There will be no ties.
Example
Input
2
Margherita 1.5 3.5 5.0
Tonno 2.0 2.5 5.5
Output
Margherita 22cm
Tonno 26cm
